title: Baked Cauliflower Mac and Cheese with Smoked Sausage
conventions: buy strings are cook measures (what goes in the pot), grams derived FROM the printed measure via db\densities.json (or the flagged USDA/label unit weights where densities has no row) so the two agree by construction; quantities quantized to house quarters, drift from the exact 3.5x scale noted per line where it exceeds 5%.

ingredients.source_raw: 16 ounces cauliflower chopped into macaroni sized pieces
ingredients.buy: 3 1/2 lb, chopped into macaroni-sized pieces (about 3 medium heads)
ingredients.notes: FRESH cauliflower to the fresh cauliflower commodity (unit each, 4 of 7 stores, cheapest Fareway $1.98/each); frozen-cauliflower-florets would be a form-flip and was not used. Source states a WEIGHT, exact 3.5x = 56 oz = 3.5 lb = 1588 g, zero drift. Head count from the proposed ~540 g medium-head figure (chicken-bacon-ranch densities followup); densities.json still has NO Cauliflower row (FLAGGED again). Food-DB row already exists (USDA raw, added 2026-08-15 this run).

ingredients.buy: 3 lb, sliced into thin rounds (about three and a half 14 oz ropes)
ingredients.notes: Generic smoked sausage is the PORK/BEEF rope class: board commodity kielbasa (label 'Kielbasa / Smoked Sausage', include /smoked\s+sausage/, excludes chicken and turkey), 7 of 7 stores, cheapest Walmart $2.336/lb; today's cells are Eckrich/Bar-S/Kroger/Johnsonville pork-beef product, and the Family Fare cell is the exact 14 oz Eckrich skinless rope this recipe describes. Deliberately NOT the existing Smoked Turkey Sausage map entry (smoked-turkey-sausage): turkey is a different variety AND roughly half the calories per oz - mapping to it would deflate a card that must sit in a 400-650 band (fresh-is-not-frozen / variety-pricing rejection class). Main protein anchored by an explicit source WEIGHT (14 oz), not an each-count. Exact 3.5x = 49 oz = 3.0625 lb, quantized 3 lb = 1361 g (-2.0%). NEW food-DB row added (Eckrich label via USDA branded mirror: 2 oz = 180 cal / 6 P / 4 C / 15 F).

Exact 3.5x = 7/8 cup, not quarter-quantizable (0.75 or 1.0 are both ~14% off), so printed as the composite 3/4 cup plus 2 tbsp = 14 tbsp = 210 g at densities 15 g/tbsp (+0.8% vs exact 208 g). Board 7 of 7, cheapest Sam's $0.1162/floz.

ingredients.buy: 7 oz, room temperature (an 8 oz brick minus 2 tbsp)
ingredients.notes: FULL-FAT cream cheese; deliberately NOT the 1/3 Fat Cream Cheese map entry (different product and macros - deflating calories matters on a card with a calorie floor). Exact 3.5x = 7 oz = 198 g, zero drift. cream-cheese commodity 7 of 7 stores, cheapest Sam's $0.1381/oz. Food-DB row already exists (USDA full-fat, added 2026-08-15 this run).

ingredients.buy: 5 1/4 cups grated, divided (3 1/2 cups in, 1 3/4 cups on top)
ingredients.notes: ingredient-map entry Cheddar Cheese, Shredded -> cheddar-cheese-shredded; board field is 'recipe' because the id is present in grocery\recipe-commodities.json (membership rule) - NOTE the earlier chicken-bacon-ranch mapped file booked this same id as 'weekly', one of the two files is off and this one follows the stated rule. Exact 3.5x = 5.25 cups, quarter-clean, zero drift; 593 g at densities 113 g/cup. Known board defects on the generic term path still present today, see board_defects_observed. Divided per source ratio (1 cup in / 1/2 cup on top).

No dedicated monterey-jack commodity exists; the board's own shredded-cheese commodity ('Shredded / Block Cheese') explicitly includes /(cheddar|mozzarella|colby|monterey|jack)\s+cheese/ in one price class, so this is a board-sanctioned class match, not a variety stretch (7 of 7 stores, cheapest Sam's $0.1521/oz). Exact 3.5x = 1.167 cups; 1.25 cups would drift +7.1%, so printed as 1 cup plus 3 tbsp = 19 tbsp = 134 g at 113 g/cup (+1.8%). NEW food-DB row added (USDA Cheese, monterey per 100 g). Densities has no Monterey Jack row (FLAGGED; used the USDA cup shredded = 113 g, identical to the cheddar row).

ingredient-map entry Cajun Seasoning -> cajun-seasoning, 7 of 7 stores, cheapest Hy-Vee $0.0833/oz. Exact 3.5x = 3.5 tsp = 10.5 g at densities 3 g/tsp, rounded 11. FLAG: densities says 3 g/tsp but the Tony Chachere's DB row implies 4.4 g/tsp (1/4 tsp = 1.1 g) - the pair disagrees; macro impact is zero (label is 0 cal) so not chased here, but noted in densities_followups.

db_entries_added: Smoked Sausage (Eckrich/Armour-Eckrich skinless pork-beef rope, USDA branded mirror: 2 oz / 56 g = 180 cal / 6 P / 4 C / 15 F, 490 mg Na)
Monterey Jack Cheese (USDA Cheese, monterey, per 100 g: 373 cal / 24.5 P / 0.7 C / 30.3 F; 1 cup shredded = 113 g)

macro_cross_check.verdict: Protein PASS (-4.3%), portions are right; every line is anchored by an explicit source weight or volume, no each-weight assumptions anywhere (the florentine failure mode cannot occur here). Calorie gap +9.3% runs HIGH, direction explained by the honest Eckrich smoked-sausage row (180 cal/2 oz; back-computing the source's own 588 implies its calculator booked a lighter ~145 cal/2 oz generic entry) and the USDA full-fat cream cheese basis. CALLED OUT LOUDLY: the band pass is TIGHT - 642 cal against a 650 ceiling is 8 cal of headroom, and the verdict is sausage-row sensitive (a Hillshire-class 170 cal/2 oz label computes ~620; a heavier andouille-class label would breach). The Eckrich row is the right anchor (it is the named product in 3 of 7 board cells including the exact 14 oz rope), but the auditor should know one row choice decides this band.
macro_cross_check.band_check: computed 642.4 cal in [400, 650] PASS with only 8 cal headroom (flagged above); carbs 16.0 g <= 35 PASS (source net carbs 8 g)
